item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong, quantified evidence that violence, deaths, displacement, or kidnapping materially fell nationwide in 2024. I also did not find clear evidence that communal, ethnic, or sectarian violence was substantially reduced across the year. Most available evidence is event-driven, especially around the August protests and Boko Haram-related vulnerability, rather than a clean year-over-year safety trend.","evidence":[{"title":"Tinubu launches national resettlement scheme for conflict victims","publisher":"State House","date":"July 6, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/","summary":"Tinubu launched a resettlement scheme for conflict victims and framed it as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is a positive anti-neglect signal, though it is administrative intent rather than evidence of measurable safety gains.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7","3B.9"]},{"title":"Tinubu establishes national education data system and approves skill development nationwide","publisher":"State House","date":"April 18, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-national-education-data-system-and-approves-skill-development-for-all-levels-of-education-teacher-s-training-and-support-nationwide/","summary":"Tinubu approved child-focused education measures, including “academic security” and out-of-school-children interventions. This is positive for long-run safety of children, but it is indirect relative to violence reduction.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7"]},{"title":"Tinubu launches education campaign, says no child should be excluded from learning","publisher":"State House","date":"May 13, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/","summary":"Tinubu backed women’s rights, anti-GBV policy, and girls’ education in safe environments. This is positive evidence for protection of vulnerable groups, though it is still programmatic rhetoric.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7"]},{"title":"Tinubu asks protesters to suspend demonstrations, seeks dialogue","publisher":"TheCable","date":"August 4, 2024","url":"https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-tinubu-asks-protesters-to-suspend-demonstrations-seeks-dialogue/","summary":"Tinubu asked protesters to pause demonstrations to create room for dialogue. This is a real de-escalatory move, but it was reactive and did not prevent the violence that followed.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.8","3B.9"]},{"title":"Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom","publisher":"Reuters via Investing.com","date":"July 31, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462","summary":"The government publicly offered dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence: some restraint, but also coercive preparedness that undercut the safety signal.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.8","3B.9","3B.5"]},{"title":"President Tinubu calls for suspension of sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso","publisher":"State House","date":"February 24, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/","summary":"Tinubu urged negotiation and a “better path” over adversarial escalation in the ECOWAS crisis. This is strong evidence of punitive escalation and collective punishment after a spontaneous domestic flare-up.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.9"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Protesters charged with treason","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"September 6, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason","summary":"HRW said protesters, including children, were held for long periods with due-process concerns. This is strong evidence that domestic insecurity was not reduced in a rights-protective way.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.1","3B.2","3B.8","3B.9"]},{"title":"Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"April 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk","summary":"HRW said Nigerian authorities had failed to sustain measures for safe learning environments, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. This is negative evidence for the claim that Tinubu left children safer from preventable insecurity.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Girls failed by authorities after escaping Boko Haram captivity","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"June 9, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/","summary":"Amnesty found that girls and young women who escaped Boko Haram captivity faced unlawful detention and weak reintegration support. This is strong evidence against a broad safety improvement for vulnerable groups.","question_ids":["3B.10","3B.7","3B.2"]}]}
